title: Rabbi Yehuda bar Ami
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in several places in the Talmud in connection with one statement that he said in the name of Rav Yehuda: a beit ha-peras that was trodden down is pure, in Eruvin 30b, Ketubot 21b, Bekhorot 29b, Niddah 57. And in Berakhot 19b the reading is Rav Yehuda bar Ashi in the name of Rav, and in Pesachim 92b the reading is Rav Yehuda bar Abaye, and in Chagigah 24b R' Chiyya bar Abba in the name of Ulla, and in Moed Katan 5b Rav Yehuda bar Ami in the name of Ulla. Hyman reports that in all these places Dikdukei Soferim records that the text should read R' Yehuda bar Ami in the name of Rav Yehuda, and he states that this is the reading in all the manuscripts.

And in the Yerushalmi, Terumot end of chapter 2, R' Yuda bar Immi in the name of R"L; Hyman says it appears that he was from Eretz Israel. Likewise in Eruvin 28b: Rabbi Zeira, when he was weakened from study, would go and sit at the entrance of Rav Yehuda bar Ami; and in Berakhot 28a: Rabbi Zeira, when he was weakened from study, would go and sit at the entrance of the house of Rabbi Natan bar Tovi. Rabbi Natan bar Tovi came out and asked him, 'Who stated a halakha in the study hall?' He said to him, 'Thus said Rabbi Yochanan.' Hyman infers from this that Rabbi Zeira was then in Eretz Israel and sat before Rabbi Yochanan.

He is also mentioned in Bereshit Rabbah 22:7, where they said: Over what were Cain and Abel disputing? Yehuda bar Ami said: over the first Eve; and there, at the end of chapter 26, Yehuda bar R' Ami; and Hyman reports that in Tanchuma Vaera 8 Yehuda bar Ami says the staff weighed sixty se'ah and was made of sanpironon, etc. He is likewise mentioned in Tanchuma Emor 7. Hyman considers it highly plausible that he was the son of the well-known R' Ami.

notes.text: מטה here is a staff. The supplied60seah and sanpironon material are preserved; the staff account remains unmatched at Vaera8 in the named Torat Emet digital edition.
Zeira and Yochanan are fully named in the connected paragraph. The rival patronymics/transmitters, all-manuscripts report and possible son-of-Ami conclusion remain Hyman’s comparisons and claims.

The actual William Davidson paragraphs of Eruvin 28b and Berakhot 28a explicitly name Rabbi Zeira, Rav Yehuda bar Ami, Rabbi Natan bar Tovi, and Rabbi Yochanan at the corresponding occurrences. Berakhot makes Natan bar Tovi come out and ask the question. Hyman’s rival transmission chains, Dikdukei Soferim and all-manuscripts assertion, Eretz Israel inference, and highly plausible son-of-Ami conclusion remain his claims; they are not new teacher, residence, or genealogical identifications. The uncollated abbreviated occurrences remain R' or R"L. The complete Torat Emet Tanchuma Vaera 8 read here includes a staff image but not the supplied sixty-se'ah/sanpironon account or its attribution; this is a bounded nonmatch, not absence elsewhere or a locator correction. All supplied numerals, Niddah 57 without an amud, the material, and the p004 source hold are retained.

Hyman’s printed notice (II, p. 554) gives sixty se’ah. Buber’s Tanchuma, Vaera 8, gives forty se’ah and attributes the sapphire staff description to Rabbi Yehuda bar Ami. The parallel in Buber’s Tazria 10 also gives forty, with the shorter attribution Rabbi Yehuda. The earlier Torat Emet check concerned a different edition of Vaera 8. Bereshit Rabbah 22:7 separately names Yehuda bar Ami in the first-Eve interpretation. The consulted Moed Katan 5b gives the ruling about a trodden beit ha-peras in Ulla’s name. Hyman’s preferred chain and statement about all manuscripts remain his report. The Zeira episodes in Eruvin 28b and Berakhot 28a feature different doorways, and neither establishes Hyman’s residence or genealogy conjecture.
